findings.issue: The arm stack is internally inconsistent: every bench loop interleaves G1ArmActionClient gestures (shrug 15/99 in CONFIRM, wave/heart/handshake on request) with rt/arm_sdk reach/present trajectories, but arm_sdk only works with the arm action service switched OFF, and that service is the gesture service itself.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/05_02_arm_action_interface.md: 如需通过 /arm_sdk 话题自主开发上肢动作，必须先关闭宇树内置的手臂控制服务 ... 服务名称为 g1_arm_example; the same page says ExecuteAction(int) is 阻塞执行 (blocking), so a 15-then-99 shrug cannot fit the plan's 1.5 s grace window either. The plan's spike 10 switches g1_arm_example off for replay and never schedules switching it back on, nor tests what the arm service does to the arm pose on re-enable, nor how long a ServiceSwitch round trip takes mid-demo. unitree_sdk2py exposes ServiceSwitch only via b2/go2 RobotStateClient (unitree_sdk2py/b2/robot_state/robot_state_client.py:57), untested on the G1 here.
findings.fix: Pick one arm owner before Monday. Simplest: arm_sdk owns the arms for the whole demo (service off at preflight, on at shutdown); author wave/heart/present as joint-space poses replayed through the same trajectory player (they are 1-2 keyframes each), and drop ExecuteAction and the shrug. If preset gestures must stay, confine them to a separate GESTURE state that does an explicit, timed ServiceSwitch on/off, measure the switch time and arm pose jump on Monday spike 5, and never call them inside PICK/HANDOVER.

findings.issue: The schedule has zero slack and serializes three work streams through one robot, one GPU and one robotics novice: ORDER→pick→handover end-to-end on the stand is due Tuesday (the same day the reach is first recorded, the camera first opened and the Orin server first used for audio), the first standing reach with a can is Wednesday, the 30-trial table Thursday, freeze Friday noon. Any one-day slip (a fall, a missing headset, a toolchain problem, a firmware gate) silently removes the rack tier and the numbers board.
findings.evidence: Plan §7 Tue row requires R1 recording on the robot, R2 running the language table and the thermal soak on the robot's GPU, and R3 running end-to-end on the same robot and server; CLAUDE.md: 'Benchmarks are serial and GPU-exclusive: never run two inference jobs at once'. The plan rejects Show Me Once at '170-220 person-hours' (§12) yet carries the same loop plus a memory tier, a stage walk, an XVF3800 DOA integration, three pick tiers and an 8-language table; a rough sum of its own work items (Orin build and tables ~12 h, ears/mouth/LED/PTT ~8 h, brain.py with recoveries/demo_mode/preflight ~20 h, gates scoring ~8 h, language clips ~10 h, memory ~8 h, brain view ~8 h, loco+lidar+bearing ~12 h, arm record/convert/replay/trials ~24 h, hands ~6 h, integration/debug ~30 h, trials/numbers/video ~16 h) is ~160-180 engineering hours before any rehearsal, i.e. all of three skilled people's week, with every robot-bound item on R1's critical path. R1 is also away at Arm Create Mon 11:00-14:30 on the first day the robot is on.
findings.fix: Cut scope today, not at the 20:00 gates (which fire after the day is spent): drop the memory tier, the XVF3800 DOA, the stage walk and languages beyond en/zh/es (plus any with a native speaker on the team). Publish a robot-time schedule in 2-hour blocks (R1 arm work, R2 GPU measurements, R3 integration) and have R3 integrate against mocked skills until the Wednesday block. Move the end-to-end-on-stand target to Wednesday 12:00 and the 30-trial table to Thursday-Friday morning; keep Friday 12:00 freeze.

findings.issue: The pick trajectories will be recorded under one controller and replayed under a much softer one: xr_teleoperate's G1_23 arm controller tracks with kp 300/80/40, while the plan replays over arm_sdk with the official example's kp 60/kd 1.5. With a 12 cm slot pitch and a 0.37 kg can, gravity sag of a few centimetres at the hand is enough to miss the slot or the koozie. Separately, running xr_teleoperate --record without --motion puts the robot into Debug Mode, which kills ai_sport until reboot.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/xr_teleoperate/teleop/robot_control/robot_arm.py:356-361 (kp_high 300/kd 3, kp_low 80/kd 3, kp_wrist 40/kd 1.5) vs /Users/junda/robot/unitree_sdk2_python/example/g1/high_level/g1_arm7_sdk_dds_example.py:74-75 (kp 60, kd 1.5), which the plan's spike 10 copies ('kp 60/kd 1.5'). teleop_hand_and_arm.py:143-144 calls motion_switcher.Enter_Debug_Mode() unless --motion; robot_arm.py:17-18,89-92 publishes to rt/lowcmd in debug mode and rt/arm_sdk only in motion mode; brief: 'Debug mode (L2+R2) kills the ai_sport service until reboot'. The plan's Tuesday row says only 'xr_teleoperate --record', not --motion, and lists the Quest as an open question with no fallback timing.
findings.fix: Record only with --motion in FSM 500 on the stand (the arms then already go through rt/arm_sdk), and make the replay engine the same G1_23_ArmController class in motion_mode=True with its own gains, feeding it the recorded joint targets at 30-50 Hz with the velocity clamp; do not re-implement the publisher with example gains. On Tuesday log commanded vs measured q with the can in hand and record the sag; tune the rack height to the loaded pose, not the unloaded one. If no headset is available by Monday night, hand-author 3 keyframes per slot with the same controller and spend Tuesday on that instead.

findings.issue: The headline (one Gemma 4 turn hears audio, sees the rack and emits order() on the Orin) is unverified on three independent axes, and the Monday 14:00 gate that retires it depends on an unverified toolchain: nobody has run Gemma 4 audio on an Orin NX, image+audio+tools in one turn is untested even on the Mac, and whether PC2 has the CUDA toolkit (nvcc) needed for the native build is unknown.
findings.evidence: Brief, prior-art corrections: 'Nobody has demonstrated Gemma 4 audio on an Orin NX ... every llama.cpp audio report is x86 CUDA or Apple Metal; NVIDIA's recipe flags an undated E2B audio problem'. Gemma digest open question: 'Audio + image in the same Gemma 4 turn on llama.cpp (mixed mmproj) is documented but untested here'. Fact-checker: 'multilingual S2TT on E2B was poor in a one-shot Spanish trial'. NVIDIA's llama.cpp container is text-only (no mmproj), so a container is not an audio fallback. The local pc2-root-fs is not a filesystem copy (only g1-doc.json, init, init-d, unitree), so nothing here shows nvcc/cuda-toolkit on PC2; Unitree's PC2 image may ship L4T without the toolkit, and installing it needs internet and GBs. The plan's Monday row also needs the robot powered on at 09:00 while the owner leaves for San Jose.
findings.fix: Tonight: run the Sunday Mac spike with the exact ORDER payload (image, text, input_audio last, tools, thinking off) and keep its requests.jsonl as the reference. Monday 09:00 first command on PC2: nvcc --version, dpkg -l | grep -i cuda-toolkit, nvpmodel -q, df -h; if the toolkit is missing, build llama.cpp inside the pinned JetPack-6 CUDA container (b9066-r36.4.tegra-aarch64-cu129-22.04, pre-pulled Sunday with the owner's approval) rather than apt-installing JetPack on the robot. Make plan B (audio-only tool turn, then the existing vision turns) the design default in brain.py now so the state machine does not change shape when plan A fails; plan A becomes a config flag flipped only after the Orin table exists.

findings.issue: The multilingual promise cannot be validated by the team as planned: the Tuesday '≥9/10 per language on the real mic' table needs native speakers for 6-8 languages, which a 3-4 person team of unknown skills does not have; synthetic or non-native clips do not predict accented native speech in a hall; and language identification from audio (the `language` enum that drives the confirmation voice, the headline twist) is not measured anywhere.
findings.evidence: Plan §3 promises confirmation 'in that language' and §7 Tue gate 'promised languages (≥9/10 only)'; §5 token table lists Piper voices for en/es/pt/fr/de/it/zh plus Kokoro ja. Brief: E2B FLEURS WER 0.090 overall, 'weakest in Arabic and Chinese (CER 0.19 for E2B)', 'one secondhand report cites ~41% WER for Gemma 4 on AMI meeting audio', and the one-shot Spanish S2TT trial was poor. No digest reports E2B language-ID accuracy from audio, and the plan's language table scores order() correctness, not the language field.
findings.fix: Promise only languages with at least two native speakers available for Tuesday recording (realistically en, zh, es, maybe hi); recruit natives from the hackathon Discord or friends for 10 clips each at 2 m with crowd playback, and score item and language fields separately with n. Confirm in the detected language only if that language is in the verified set and the item is valid; otherwise confirm in English with the item name (still a correct order). Put the language table on the slide with n per language and the ones you did not verify listed as 'not tested'.

findings.issue: The camera decision rests on a false premise and an untested geometry: the plan buys a chest-mounted C920 'to avoid the pyrealsense2 source build', but the D435i colour stream is already a plain V4L2 UVC node on PC2 (realsense-webrtc captures it without librealsense), and a chest camera is poorly placed to see the robot's own hand at the lift-to-chest pose or the rack at hand height, which every grasp and handover gate depends on.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/realsense-webrtc/README.md: 'D435i RGB sensor -> USB/UVC kernel driver -> V4L2 YUYV capture ... It intentionally does not load librealsense/pyrealsense2', with the caveat 'A V4L2 node normally has one active capture owner' (stop teleimager-realsense-webrtc/teleimager services first). Plan §6 lists the C920 at Micro Center Monday pickup and spike 7 (Tue 09:00) is the first time any frame is captured; the hand-crop gates ('Is the robot's hand holding a can?', 'Is a human hand holding the can?') are scored only Wednesday.
findings.fix: Tuesday 09:00: stop teleimager-realsense-webrtc.service and mediamtx, open the D435i node with OpenCV at 640x480 YUYV, and check from the head viewpoint that the rack at hand height and the lifted can are both in frame; keep the C920 only as a second viewpoint if the head FOV fails. Define the crop rectangles from the actual camera pose on the stand and score the four gate questions on 30 real frames each by Tuesday night, not Wednesday.

findings.issue: The handover release signal is unproven: the plan releases on Gemma's 'human hand holding the can' answer plus a BrainCo 'finger-state pull', but the hand bridge publishes only finger position and estimated current, and nothing shows that a judge pulling a koozied can out of a 50 N position-controlled grip moves either signal. The vision gate is also specified at 2 Hz on a 280-token crop that the plan itself budgets at 0.5-0.7 s per call on a single slot.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/brainco_hand_service/main.cpp:118-120 maps status->positions to q and status->currents to tau_est; the README says no tactile over the bridge. Plan §3 0:35: 'fingers open on that signal, never on a timer'; §5 gates table: hand crop 0.5-0.7 s, yet 'at 2 Hz'. The harness never measured a hand gate (LATENCY_RESULTS.md measures a fridge presence gate: 12/14 no, two false positives on wide views).
findings.fix: Monday spike 5: log q and tau_est at 100 Hz while a human pulls a can from the closed hand (and while nobody does) and decide from the trace whether a pull threshold exists. If not, release on two consecutive vision 'yes' answers on the 70-token full frame at ~1 Hz plus a spoken 'take it', opening to 0.4 first so the can can slide out while the fingers still cradle it; log every release decision with the frame for the numbers board.

findings.issue: The latency budget is built on unmeasured pieces and ignores prefix-cache thrash: the ORDER estimate assumes the audio encoder is free, the 280-token crop has never been timed (the harness measured only 70- and 150-token frames), and alternating five call types with different system/tool prefixes (ORDER, gates, box_2d, captioner, memory verify) on one slot loses the cached prefix on every call.
findings.evidence: LATENCY_RESULTS.md: vision encoder 58 ms at 70 tokens, 135 ms at 150 tokens (Mac), nothing at 280; 'alternating request types with different system text would pay part of the cold cost'; cold vs warm on the Mac 410→324 ms (tool) and 246→222 ms (one word); Orin section 'not measured', vision encoder 0.7-2.5x the Mac assumed. Plan §5 projects ORDER 1.0-1.5 s with '≤200 audio (8 s at 25 tok/s)' tokens through a 12-block conformer whose Orin cost no source reports (only the Orin Nano Super 0.37-0.56 s TTFT with unknown clip length). Plan §5 gates '~40 cached' vs ORDER '~300 cached' confirms different prefixes.
findings.fix: Use one identical system message and tools block for every call type (the per-call question goes after the image, which the harness showed is where it must be anyway), so the prefix stays warm across ORDER, gates and box calls; measure on Monday: 3 s and 8 s audio clips, 70- vs 280-token frames, cold vs warm, and write the Orin table before the UI timings are fixed. Budget the LED/voice cover for 2.5 s and set the gate loop to ~1 Hz on 70-token frames unless Wednesday's scoring proves the crop is needed.

findings.issue: Battery runtime does not cover the judging window: the G1 is rated about 2 h, the GPU will be busy all day, the bench loop needs locked stand (arm_sdk requires FSM 500/501, so Damp between groups saves little), and the second battery is only 'ask, price unverified' with the swap already scheduled at 12:30.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/00_about_G1.md: 续航时间 约2h; brief: 'with the GPU busy expect less'; plan §6 'Second G1 battery | ask | price unverified' and §3 'battery swap around 12:30'; judging runs 10:00-15:00+ with the stage after. No charging-while-operating path is documented.
findings.fix: Email Unitree and a reseller Sunday for a spare with a Friday delivery date, and ask the organizers whether another G1 team will be present (loaner); measure real runtime in Tuesday's 30-minute soak (rt/lowstate battery fields) and extrapolate. If no spare arrives, plan the bench loop in two 75-minute windows around a 90-minute charge, during which the robot sits in Damp on the stand doing voice turns and LED/speech only, and say so on the card.

findings.issue: The stage walk is a fourth subsystem (LocoClient pulses, box_2d bearing on crowd frames, a Livox point-cloud guard, and an arm held via arm_sdk while stepping) with 10 trials on Thursday only, it contradicts the plan's own rule 'arms extend only in locked stand, never while stepping', and its lidar topic name is wrong, a sign nothing was prototyped.
findings.evidence: Plan §5 'guard: rt/utlidar/cloud_livox_mid ±30°' vs /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/04_06_lidar_services_interface.md: 'rt/utlidar/cloud_livox_mid360' at 10 Hz; §9 'Arms extend only in locked stand, never while stepping' vs §3 stage 1:00-2:00 'Pick, then the only walk of the day ... handover'. Brief: LocoClient Move may return 0 with no motion on some firmware (issue #170 pattern), gated Monday; xr_teleoperate --motion does walk with arms held, so it is possible but untested here.
findings.fix: Make the stationary stage the default script now (volunteer walks to the robot) and treat the walk as a Thursday-afternoon bonus only if gate 1 passed, the bench loop is frozen, and a PointCloud2 subscriber on rt/utlidar/cloud_livox_mid360 has been shown to stop Move within 0.5 s at 0.7 m on ten tries; walk with the can held at the chest (hand already closed), never with the arm extended.

findings.issue: Memory and side-integration numbers are understated: the llama-server figure of 4.5-5 GB is below the one on-Orin audio report, and the XVF3800 direction-of-arrival needs vendor USB control-message integration that the plan treats as 'free'.
findings.evidence: Cached files: E2B UD-Q4_K_XL 2.62 GB + mmproj-BF16 0.99 GB (~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--unsloth--gemma-4-E2B-it-qat-GGUF); brief: the Orin Nano Super community project ran native E2B audio 'in a 5.7 GiB GPU budget'; add litert-lm serve 1-1.5 GB, mediamtx/teleimager and the BrainCo bridge, leaving roughly 3-5 GB, not more. The plan's 'XVF3800 (DOA only)' line and 'free turn toward the speaker yaw pulse' have no integration hours anywhere in §7 or §8.
findings.fix: Budget 6 GB for llama-server in the Tuesday soak, stop the teleimager/mediamtx services during the demo, and keep the 2.5 GB-free threshold. Cut the DOA feature (and the XVF3800 purchase unless it is the backup capture mic); the DJI/Lark handheld stick with push-to-talk is the whole audio path.

verdict: As written, this plan is not working on Oct 23: the arm stack is internally inconsistent (gesture service on versus arm_sdk off; trajectories recorded at kp 300 and replayed at kp 60), the headline one-turn multilingual order is unverified on the Orin, on the Mac in mixed form, and on native speakers, and the schedule pushes three streams through one robot, one GPU and one robotics novice with no slack. The core idea is still the right one for Track 2 and can win if it is shrunk to what the harness already supports: a push-to-talk voice order (plan A or B), a recorded arm_sdk pick from a rack, and a vision-gated handover with honest per-stage numbers. The single change that matters most is to decide today that arm_sdk is the only arm owner and to cut the memory tier, the DOA, the stage walk and the 8-language table now, so Tuesday and Wednesday belong entirely to the pick and the handover gates.

findings.issue: Gemma does not actually decide which can: the pick is a taped slot chosen in code, the item enum contradicts the planted 'blue can' negative, and one judge swapping two cans exposes the loop as a macro.
findings.evidence: Plan §3: 'a 3-slot can rack ... taped relative to the feet marks' and '`pick(slot=2)`: recorded rt/arm_sdk reach'; nothing in §3 or §5 derives slot from the image, so 'looks at the rack, decides which can you meant' (§2) is the item enum, not perception. §5 tool table: `order.item` is 'enum of the cans on the rack today (red_can, green_can, blue_can)' while §3 1:15 stages 'the judge orders a colour that is not on the rack; the presence gate answers no' — a colour not on the rack is not in the enum, so it becomes `other` → English ask-back, not the rehearsed negative. Harness LATENCY_RESULTS.md lines 137-138: presence gate 78/78 yes but 12/14 no, both false positives on wide views, so even the planted negative can misfire and the code then has no slot to pick. Brief (judging digest): judges penalize 'a Gemma that could be swapped for any model' and verify the tech is 'not just faked for the demo'; the AGI House robotics crowd 'discounts controlled-setting clips'.
findings.fix: Make the slot a per-order Gemma perception decision: after `order()`, ask one direct question after a fresh rack frame ('Which slot holds the green can? 1/2/3/none') or run box_2d on the rack and compute the slot in code (the harness's strongest path, 100% box detection). Make the enum a superset (red/green/blue/none) so 'blue' reaches the presence gate, and make 'item not found' a code branch independent of the gate (gate false-positive → slot none → honest negative, never a pick). Add 'judge swaps two cans' as a listed bench test with its own row in the Thursday success table and invite judges to do it.

findings.issue: The no-cloud proof covers PC2 only; the robot's PC1 carries Unitree's cloud client (MQTT OTA/fault upload, WebRTC signalling) and performs network time sync whenever the robot is in Wi-Fi mode, and `tailscale down` leaves tailscaled able to reconnect.
findings.evidence: g1-docs 02_01_architecture_description.md line 15 ('用户授权后，G1 才会连接云服务'), lines 31/40 (OTA module uses MQTT to the cloud server for fault upload, upgrades and WebRTC signalling), line 50 (PC1 is Unitree's closed computer; developers only get PC2). 04_09_time_sync_interface.md line 11: '每次将G1设置为WiFi模式时，该时钟源都会进行网络授时' — PC1 does network time sync every time the G1 is put in Wi-Fi mode. Plan §5 'On-device, verifiably' lists `ip route` on PC2, `sudo tailscale down`, the unplugged WAN cable and the AP — all PC2-side; PC1's Wi-Fi mode is never mentioned, and §7 Mon has 'R2 via Tailscale from 09:00' on the same box. Brief (G1 corrections): 'keep the Unitree app (cloud MQTT/WebRTC) out of the judged loop'. Hackathon facts: 'no cloud anywhere in the loop' is the one hard rule.
findings.fix: Extend preflight.sh and the radios panel to the whole robot: robot Wi-Fi mode off or AP-only (set in the app, photographed, then app disconnected and phone BLE off), `ip neigh`/`arp` on 192.168.123.0/24 showing no gateway, PC1 unreachable to any public address (ssh PC1 if credentials exist, else the app's network page), `sudo systemctl stop tailscaled && disable` instead of `tailscale down`, and the MacBook on the robot AP only (no venue Wi-Fi, no venue Ethernet). Add 'the robot's own computer PC1 has no uplink' to the slide's no-cloud evidence.

findings.issue: 'Mic not in wake mode' does not silence the factory voice service: it keeps listening and breathes the LED blue on any human voice, L2+Select on the spotter's remote starts factory recording, and the plan's LED grammar reuses the same blue/green the factory uses.
findings.evidence: g1-docs 01_03_voice_assistant_instructions.md line 29: '未唤醒时听到人声会蓝灯呼吸，唤醒后收到指令会绿灯呼吸' (not woken: a human voice makes the LED breathe blue; woken: green) — the plan's §3 grammar is 'LED blue while listening ... LED green' after `order()`, so a judge's voice will trigger the factory blue breathing alongside ours. Line 41: long-pressing L2+Select records and force-feeds audio to the recognition framework. Lines 43-44: '关闭交互: 程序休眠，停止录音，关闭后即不会产生隐私问题' — only 'close interaction' stops recording. Plan §5 says only 'the mic stays out of wake mode' and the §3 privacy card promises 'no continuous recording'. Brief (G1 corrections): the offline assistant 'still wakes on 笨笨同学 / L2+Select, speaks, drives the LEDs'. Also 01_01_remote_control.md lines 131-133, 190: SELECT+Y/A/X fire wave/shake/turn-and-wave presets and SELECT+right stick drives the waist — one slip by the spotter is an unscripted motion on stage. (Side note: 04_05_VuiClient_Service.md lines 53-54 document the built-in ASR/TTS as 本地离线 local offline, so the plan's 'TtsMaker execution location is undocumented' is off; harmless since Piper is used.)
findings.fix: Put the voice service into 关闭交互 (sleep) in preflight.sh and verify by speaking at the robot while watching the LED (no blue breathing); if it cannot be set from PC2, do it in the app before disconnecting and re-verify after every reboot/battery swap. Choose LED colours the factory never uses (e.g., magenta = listening, white = thinking, green only after our confirmation) and keep Monday's contention test. Physically guard the remote: tape over Select, A, X, Y and the right stick; spotter's thumbs rest on L2 and B only. Correct the privacy card to what is true after sleep is confirmed.

findings.issue: The Best-Use-of-LiteRT bet is token use: EmbeddingGemma 2 embeds rows that are three enum values plus a language code (a SQL WHERE, not retrieval), the 'transcript' it is supposed to embed does not exist, and 'remembers who asked for what' overclaims identity the robot never stores.
findings.evidence: Plan §5 memory write: 'every transcript as Gemma returned it, every tool call, a ≤12-word rack caption' — but the ORDER turn returns only `order(item, language)` with thinking off (§5 ORDER row, 15-20 output tokens); no transcript is produced, and adding a free-text argument fights the brief's Pixel-digest finding that tool-call success collapses with argument count and CLAUDE.md's 'validate client-side'. Rows therefore reduce to {red|green|blue} × language. Brief hackathon facts: the page says 'Use LiteRT-LM to run Gemma locally'; judging digest: 'whether Best Use of LiteRT requires LiteRT on the primary device or counts a LiteRT-LM component' is an open question; fact-check: 'Do not build a plan that needs stacking to pay off' — yet §4 books EV $1.0k that 'depends entirely on stacking'. Competing entries (Reachy-style Pi 5, Pixel) will run Gemma 4 itself on LiteRT-LM. One-liner and winners sentence (§2): 'remembers who asked for what' while the privacy card says 'no faces'.
findings.fix: Gate it on the organizers' written answer by Monday 20:00. If a secondary LiteRT-LM component counts: make the memory real — after the pick, off the critical path, run one cheap text-only turn that writes a ≤12-word description of the request (language, item, any spoken detail) and embed that plus the rack caption so recall is semantic and cross-lingual; change every surface to 'remembers what was ordered'. If the answer is no, unclear, or the team is three people: cut the memory tier and every LiteRT mention, spend the half day on pick/handover reliability, and never claim 'Best Use of LiteRT' while Gemma 4 runs on llama.cpp.

findings.issue: The project's identity ('no speech recognizer', 'Any Language') is hostage to Monday's unverified Orin audio spike, and plan C silently changes both the language set and the story without a written plan-C pitch.
findings.evidence: Plan §1 risk one and §9 row 1: plan C = sherpa-onnx Parakeet, 'the single-model line goes'. Brief (prior-art digest): Parakeet v3 covers '25 European languages, not streaming' — no zh/ja/hi/ko/ar, while the plan's Piper list includes zh and the stage line promises Portuguese or Hindi. Brief corrections (prior art): 'Nobody has demonstrated Gemma 4 audio on an Orin NX'; Gemma corrections: multilingual S2TT on E2B 'was poor in a one-shot Spanish trial'. Under plan C the entry becomes the 2025 Jetson prize shape (ASR + Gemma + Piper, judging digest) with a humanoid, and the name becomes false.
findings.fix: Write the plan-C story now, in full: name, one-liner, two sentences, the slide line 'Parakeet ASR → Gemma 4 decides', and a plan-C language table (European via Parakeet, or a Whisper-class multilingual model via sherpa-onnx if zh/ja are promised). Tuesday's gate then picks between two complete stories. Keep the Mac result as evidence that Gemma hears natively, but say 'on the Mac, not yet on the robot' and only if the organizers allow a tethered Mac in writing (§10).

findings.issue: Stage lines quote numbers and facts that are unmeasured or untrue: 'under half a second per look', 'a second and a half', 'nothing in this room has an internet connection', 'twelve days after its release', 'two billion parameters', 'every number ... measured on this robot this week'.
findings.evidence: Plan §2 story vs §5 table: gates are projected 0.3-0.45 s but '0.5-0.7 s on the crop', and §3 runs the can-in-hand and hand-on-can gates on 280-token crops, so 'under half a second per look' is false for the looks that decide the handover; the §5 table is labelled 'projection until Monday' and CLAUDE.md warns 'Mac numbers are not Orin numbers'. 'Nothing in this room has an internet connection' — a hundred phones. §4: EmbeddingGemma 2 'twelve days after its release' — brief: released Oct 6; Oct 24 is 18 days. 'Two billion parameters' — E2B is effective-2B; the cached Q4 GGUF + mmproj set is ~3.6 GB (brief line 38), far more than a true 2B model at 4 bits, and the Gemma-team judges know the distinction. Brief judging digest: judges verify the tech is 'not just faked' and praise 'detailed on-device benchmarks'.
findings.fix: Strip every number from the stage script and leave typed slots ('__ s to understand you, __ ms per look, n = __') that R4 fills Friday from the final Orin table; say 'nothing in this loop'; say 'Gemma 4 E2B, the two-billion-effective-parameter model'; drop the days-since-release line; keep 'measured on this robot' only for rows with Orin n on the slide.

findings.issue: 'Scripted skills, Gemma decisions, zero teleop' conceals that the reach and present poses are teleoperation recordings replayed open-loop, which is exactly the thing robotics judges probe for.
findings.evidence: Plan §7 Tue: 'Record reach-to-slot x3, present pose and holster reach by xr_teleoperate `--record`'; §12: 'the record-and-replay machinery ... is exactly how our reach and present poses are built'; §3 stage closing sentence: 'Scripted skills, Gemma decisions, zero teleop.' Brief judging digest: the AGI House robotics crowd 'discounts controlled-setting clips and teleop'; prior-art digest: Tesla's We Robot and 1X NEO 'lost the room the instant teleoperation was suspected'. Being asked 'how was the reach made?' after saying 'zero teleop' reads as being caught rather than as disclosure.
findings.fix: Disclose it first and precisely, on the slide and in the closing sentence: 'Reach = one teleop-recorded trajectory replayed open-loop to a taped slot; hand close and release are sensor- and Gemma-gated; nobody teleoperates during the demo.' Label the brain-view provenance tag `[recorded skill: teleop replay]` and gestures `[Unitree preset 26]`.

findings.issue: The two-sentence story carries five features; the winners-post sentences run ~110 words and the loop adds gestures, a planted grasp failure, memory and a walk.
findings.evidence: Plan §2 'two sentences for the winners post' packs multilingual order, single-model audio, `order()` tool call, hand-gated release, EmbeddingGemma 2 on LiteRT-LM, no ASR, no cloud, Orin latencies and honest negatives; §3 bench adds gestures and memory recall, stage adds a walk. Brief judging digest: 'Glenn Cameron and Kristen Quan write the winners posts, so a project that is easy to describe in two sentences helps'; judges reward 'a working end-to-end loop' and penalize 'projects with no clear user'. The lens question — is the story clear in two sentences — fails as written.
findings.fix: One spine on every surface: 'Order a drink in your own language; one Gemma 4 model on the robot hears you, finds the can, hands it to you, and says so when it can't.' Second sentence: offline, measured, honest. Memory and gestures are bench extras and never enter the name, one-liner or stage opener unless the LiteRT answer is yes.

findings.issue: Stage 'gasp one' depends on an unbriefed Gemma-team judge speaking a Tuesday-verified language; an unverified language yields `other` and an English 'Red or green?' on stage.
findings.evidence: Plan §3 stage 0:30: 'A Gemma-team judge takes the stick and orders in their language'; §5 `order.language` is 'enum of Tuesday-verified languages plus `other`' → amber ask-back in English. Brief: E2B is weakest in Arabic and Chinese (CER 0.19); research JSON: Piper has no Japanese or Korean and the plan's Piper list omits Hindi while the stage line promises 'Portuguese or Hindi'; judge identities are behind sign-in (judging open question 'Who the six co-hosts/judges are'). A judge may also decline to perform.
findings.fix: Ask at Arm Create Monday and by email which languages the judges speak; verify exactly those Tuesday. On stage use a pre-agreed speaker (a bilingual teammate or a judge who agreed backstage) in a table language; keep 'any judge, any language' at the bench where `other` is a harmless ask-back. Print the verified-language list on the numbers board so 'any language' is honestly bounded.

findings.issue: The only walk of the day is performed on stage while holding a can in a BrainCo hand, a combination first tested Thursday, with a collapse-style e-stop as the safety net.
findings.evidence: Plan §3 stage 1:00-2:00: pick, then 'the only walk of the day: 2 m ... toward the raised hand' — walking while rt/arm_sdk holds a present pose with the can; §9: 'Arms extend only in locked stand, never while stepping'; §7 Thu 'stage walk 10x on a taped lane' is the first listed walk test and does not say it is with the can. Brief (G1 digest): rt/arm_sdk 'only works in locked-stand or run-control FSM 500/501'; a fall 'with BrainCo hands probably breaks fingers'; LocoClient is firmware-gated (issue #170); L2+B damp = the robot collapses.
findings.fix: Make 'the volunteer walks to the robot' the default stage script and the walk a bonus promoted only if Thursday logs 10/10 with the can held and IMU within Wednesday's envelope. If walking is kept, walk empty-handed first (approach), then pick from a rack beside the volunteer; never carry while stepping.

findings.issue: The privacy card and the memory design disagree: 'no faces, no continuous recording' versus per-row JPEGs from a chest camera and a 2 Hz camera loop on the judge's hand.
findings.evidence: Plan §3 card: 'no faces, no continuous recording, memory wiped at 17:00'; §5 SQLite rows store 't, text, vec, jpeg' and §3 runs the hand-on-can gate at 2 Hz on the C920 chest view; a judge leaning over the rack is in frame. Brief ('Robot That Remembers' alternative): 'a robot filming attendees all day needs sign-off'.
findings.fix: Keep no JPEG for request rows and only the rack crop for scene rows; state exactly 'camera frames are analysed live and not stored; order text is kept until 17:00 and deleted on stage'; show the deletion on the brain view at close.

findings.issue: The stage opener names a real relative and a specific Thanksgiving; if invented it is a cheap thing for a judge to catch and it contradicts the honesty posture.
findings.evidence: Plan §2 90-second story: 'My mother-in-law Yuki visited from Osaka last Thanksgiving ... sat in the corner for two hours.' Brief judging digest: judges reward human-centred stories but state an intent to verify the project is 'not just faked for the demo'; a personal anecdote later found to be fabricated costs more than it earns. The plan also lists Japanese confirmation as conditional on Kokoro passing a one-hour test, so Yuki's own language may not be in the table.
findings.fix: Use a true anecdote from any team member, or open with 'imagine' — one word — and make sure the protagonist's language is one the robot will actually answer in on Saturday.

verdict: As written this is a credible Track 2 top-three entry if Monday's Orin audio spike passes and the pick clears its gate, but it would not survive the first skeptical judge test: swap two cans and "Gemma sees the rack and decides which can" collapses into a taped-slot macro, which is the exact "swappable wrapper / faked for the demo" failure the Gemma and robotics judges screen for. The single change that matters most is to make the slot a per-order Gemma perception decision (one direct question or box_2d after a fresh rack frame, geometry in code, enum a superset with a real "none" branch) and to rehearse the can swap and the honest negative as listed bench tests. After that, close the two no-cloud gaps the preflight misses (PC1's cloud/NTP client and the factory voice service that keeps listening unless put to sleep), cut every stage number not measured on the Orin, and treat LiteRT as a yes/no organizer answer rather than a prize line.

findings.issue: The bench demo is free-standing, but the only e-stop is a fall, and the handover puts a judge inside the fall zone. The plan's two safety rules ('judges outside the tape', 'spotter on L2+B within 1.5 m') contradict the demo itself: a handover needs the judge within the ~0.45 m arm span, the release signal includes a 'finger-state pull' (the judge tugs on a balancing biped), and the standing controller steps when disturbed. Tug -> step toward judge -> spotter presses L2+B -> 35 kg falls onto the judge or the rack table, with BrainCo fingers first.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/01_00_quick_start.md:130: pressing L2+B enters damping mode and 'the device will fall because it loses balance control'. /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/01_01_remote_control.md standing-mode row: when the robot is disturbed and cannot keep balance it starts stepping. /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/00_about_G1.md:277,290 and note [6]: ~35 kg, arm span ~0.45 m, 'keep sufficient safety distance between people and the robot'. /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/01_Operational_guidance.md:12: Unitree recommends keeping G1 suspended on the protective stand for the whole of daily demos and development. Plan section 3: robot on taped feet marks inside a 2x2 m mat; section 9: 'spotter on L2+B within 1.5 m', 'judges outside the tape'.
findings.fix: Run the entire bench day with the robot clipped into its protective stand: feet on the floor in locked stand (FSM 500), strap with a few cm of slack, casters locked, so L2+B means 'hang', not 'fall'. Unitree's own arm_sdk routine says to test suspended in locked stand (05_01_arm_control_routine.md:15), so the pick and handover paths are unaffected. Hand the can across the table edge so the judge's feet stay outside the frame; release on the vision gate before any pull is needed and set the pull threshold so the judge never has to tug. Only the stage segment is free-standing, and only if Monday's walk gate passed; otherwise wheel the stand onto the stage. Give the spotter one job (L2+B), hands free, standing behind and to the side, never presenting.

findings.issue: The power budget for the day does not close. One 9000 mAh pack is rated ~2 h, less with the GPU busy; charging needs the pack out of the robot (quick-detach, 54V 5A charger, roughly 2 h to refill), so one pack cannot be charged while the robot runs. Judging is 10:00-15:00 at the bench plus stage and awards (and the brief notes past AGI House demos ran ~20:00). The plan schedules 60 bench loops (every ~5 min, 10:00-15:00) and a 12:30 swap on a second pack that is only 'ask, price unverified'.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/00_about_G1.md:300-303: 9000 mAh quick-detach battery, charger 54V 5A, runtime ~2 h. Brief, G1 digest: 'about 2 h; with the GPU busy expect less, so plan charging between judge rounds'. Brief, judging open questions: 'past AGI House build days ran demos around 20:00... plan for a hard stop at ~15:00 for judging regardless'. Plan section 6: 'Second G1 battery | ask | price unverified'; section 7 Sat row: 'bench loops every ~5 min 10:00-15:00... battery swap 12:30'; Thu row logs battery runtime only on Thursday.
findings.fix: Make the second pack a hard requirement with a Monday deadline (Unitree reseller, another Bay Area G1 owner, or a rental firm), bring the charger and secure a mains outlet at the bench so pack A charges while B runs. Measure real draw on Tuesday's soak with the full stack (not Thursday). Whatever the pack count, publish a standing-time budget: robot in Damp on the stand between groups (near-zero draw), stand up only when a group arrives, cap loops per hour, and post 'robot stands at :00 / :20 / :40' so judges come at known times instead of the robot standing idle for five hours.

findings.issue: The bench-to-stage transition is unplanned and breaks the one calibrated primitive. The pick is a recorded rt/arm_sdk reach to a rack 'taped relative to the feet marks'; moving the robot, table and rack to the stage between the top-six announcement and the slot means re-hanging and re-standing via the hanger sequence, re-taping, re-warming the server and re-establishing the rack offset in minutes, in a crowd. Friday has five timed stage rehearsals but no timed teardown-move-setup, and the stage floor (steps, rugs) is unknown.
findings.evidence: Plan section 3: rack 'taped relative to the feet marks'; section 8 spike 10: reach replayed from a recorded episode 'at the real rack height'; section 7 Fri row lists stage rehearsals and bench loops only. /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/01_00_quick_start.md:105-121: entering motion from Damp requires the hanger (L2+B, L2+UP, lower rope, R2+A, wait for stable). /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/07_debugging_specification.md:17: the protective stand has four lockable casters. /Users/junda/robot/harness/LATENCY_RESULTS.md 'Recommended request': first image request after a server start was ~2x slower (934 vs ~520 ms).
findings.fix: Build the rack as a jig referenced to the stand frame (or a foot plate the robot stands on), so the calibration travels with the stand; the stand on its casters is the dolly. Rehearse the full bench-to-stage move on Friday with a stopwatch (target under 10 minutes including stand-up sequence, warm-up request and preflight). Decide now: if the stage is up steps or on a rug, the stage demo happens at the bench and the judges walk over; say so to the organizers today.

findings.issue: The setup window is 30 minutes for a sequence that has never been timed. Doors 9:30, judging may start at 10:00; in that window the plan has two people unloading a 35 kg case, assembling the stand, hanging and booting (about 1 min boot, then the L2+B / L2+UP / lower / R2+A sequence), taping, AP, DDS on eth0, server load plus warm-up, preflight.sh and a dry run.
findings.evidence: Brief, hackathon facts: '10:00-17:00 PT, doors 9:30'. Plan section 7 Sat row: '08:00 load... 09:30 setup... one dry run before 10:00'. /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/01_00_quick_start.md:105: boot takes about one minute, then L2+B and L2+UP; :111-121: lower the rope, R2+A, wait until stable, release the hook. Brief, G1 digest: 'two people to pack; rental firms move it in a ~50 kg case in an SUV'.
findings.fix: Ask for 08:30 load-in in today's organizer email and treat 09:30 as the latest. Write a 60-minute setup checklist (case open to first loop) and time it in Friday's dress rehearsal from a packed case in a different room, including the stand assembly. Pack a second complete cable set and print the checklist; the first loop of the day is a dry run with a teammate, not a judge.

findings.issue: The LED grammar collides with the firmware's safety colours and with the factory assistant's own LED behaviour. The head LED is the spotter's only hardware status indicator (blue normal control, orange damped, yellow debug, red abnormal, purple zero torque); the plan overrides it with blue/cyan/green/amber/red brain states. Separately, the assistant's LED breathes blue whenever it hears a voice while not awake, and L2+Select wakes it in every mode, so in a loud house the head LED will flash on its own and the assistant can be triggered by a remote mis-press.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/01_01_remote_control.md LED table: normal control blue, damping orange, debug yellow, abnormal red, zero torque purple, ready dark blue. /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/01_03_voice_assistant_instructions.md: 'all modes support L2+Select wake', 'when not awake, hearing a human voice makes the LED breathe blue', '关闭交互: program sleeps, stops recording'. /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/04_05_VuiClient_Service.md:99: LedControl calls must be >200 ms apart. Plan section 5: 'led: AudioClient.LedControl (blue/cyan/green/amber/red)'; section 3: 'LED blue while listening'.
findings.fix: Leave the head LED to the firmware entirely; show the brain state on the monitor and on a cheap USB LED ring on the table, with a legend card. On Monday confirm that 关闭交互 (close interaction) is set, persists across reboot and does not block PlayStream; tape over L2+Select and L1+L2 on the R3 remote; add 'assistant asleep' to preflight.sh.

findings.issue: A foam mat under a balancing biped, and an unknown floor. The plan stands the robot on a '2x2 m foam mat' with taped feet marks; Unitree only sanctions flat hard floors, compressible foam degrades balance and shifts the recorded reach, and nobody has confirmed whether the AGI House bench area and stage are hardwood or rug.
findings.evidence: Plan section 6: 'Floor tape, 2x2 m foam mat'; section 3: 'taped feet marks inside a 2x2 m mat'. /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/01_01_remote_control.md:166: lying/squat boot 'only on flat, hard ground; other scenarios risk a fall'. Brief, G1 open questions: 'confirm the venue has a flat hard floor area roughly 3x3 m'.
findings.fix: No foam under the feet. With the robot in the stand, padding is unnecessary; if wanted, put it around the stand's perimeter. Ask the organizers today about the floor surface at the bench and on stage, and bring a 1.2 x 1.2 m plywood or MDF board as a known-flat base for both if the floor is carpet or rug.

findings.issue: The peripheral tree tethers the robot to a wall. C920, DJI receiver, PTT button, USB speaker and XVF3800 exceed PC2's three USB-C host ports, so everything hangs on a 'powered USB-C 3.0 hub' that needs mains. For the stage walk the hub must be unplugged; bus-powered, the webcam plus speaker plus receiver can brown out and re-enumerate, so /dev/video*, ALSA card and evdev names change and ears/eyes/mouth fail silently.
findings.evidence: Plan section 6: 'Powered USB-C 3.0 hub, 10 m Cat6'; section 5 architecture: DJI RX (UAC), XVF3800, PTT button (evdev), UVC C920, Piper to USB speaker (ALSA) all on PC2; section 3 stage: 'the only walk of the day: 2 m'. Brief, G1 digest: PC2 has 'three USB-C 3.0 host ports'.
findings.fix: Power the hub from a USB-C PD power bank strapped to the robot (or cut to bus-powered devices and test them unplugged), pin every device by /dev/serial/by-id, /dev/v4l/by-id and ALSA card name in preflight.sh, and run the full stack unplugged for 10 minutes on Thursday. Keep the mains cable at the bench only as a charger for the bank.

findings.issue: Gestures and the pick use two arm control paths that exclude each other, and the loop toggles between them every two minutes. Gestures go through G1ArmActionClient (the built-in g1_arm_example service); the pick and present pose go through rt/arm_sdk, which requires that service to be switched off first. The bench loop does pick -> handover -> gesture on request, so brain.py must flip ServiceSwitch each loop; a sustained gesture (heart, high five) left un-released returns 7401 and a gesture issued during another returns 7400, each of which freezes the arm in front of a judge.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/05_02_arm_action_interface.md: 'to develop upper-limb motion via /arm_sdk you must first close Unitree's built-in arm control service' (g1_arm_example via ServiceSwitch); error table 7400 'topic occupied, an action is executing', 7401 'arm is raised, use action 99 to restore', 7404 'current FSM cannot trigger this action'. Plan section 5: gestures via ExecuteAction 26/20/27/99 and arm via rt/arm_sdk in the same state machine; section 3: gesture at 1:40 after the pick at 0:12.
findings.fix: Use one control path at the bench: record the three gestures as rt/arm_sdk trajectories with the same record/replay machinery as the reach (the plan already builds it), and keep G1ArmActionClient only for the stage if the service is on there. If both must coexist, make the switch state an explicit brain.py state shown on the brain view, always send 99 before switching, and run the gesture-pick-gesture sequence 20 times on Tuesday on the stand.

findings.issue: Stage AV and the backup video are assumed, not arranged. The stage demo projects the brain view from a laptop that must stay on the robot's AP, but no one has verified the stage has an HDMI input or a PA; casting (AirPlay/Chromecast) needs the venue Wi-Fi the plan forbids; an 8 W Pebble speaker will not carry Piper's Portuguese confirmation ('gasp one') over 100 people; and the backup video is 'for a hardware fault only' with no rehearsed switch.
findings.evidence: Plan section 3 stage: 'the brain view is projected'; section 5: 'venue Wi-Fi never joined', laptop 'display only' on the robot's AP; section 6: 'Creative Pebble V3 USB speaker (the 3 W onboard speaker loses the hall)'; section 10: 'Canned video as the stage demo' excluded. Brief, judging digest gotcha (4): 'a backup video must exist'; prior-art digest: Pepper-class demos lost rooms when the audience could not tell what the robot understood.
findings.fix: Ask the organizers today: HDMI input, audio input, PA, stage size, steps. Bring HDMI and USB-C adapters plus a 3.5 mm cable so the robot's speech goes to the house PA (duplicate Piper output on the laptop over the AP, or a long 3.5 mm run from the Orin); if casting is unavoidable, laptop on Ethernet to the robot and Wi-Fi to the venue, labelled 'display only' on the slide. Cut the backup video to 90 s with captions, load it on the laptop and a phone, and rehearse the hardware-fault branch once (who says what, at which second).

findings.issue: The RF plan has three 2.4 GHz links in a 100-phone house and the most important one is the e-stop. The DJI Mic Mini and Lark M2 are both 2.4 GHz, the robot's USB AP defaults to a crowded band, and the R3 remote link is the only e-stop; the robot has an explicit 'remote feedback data timeout' error state, and what the controller does on remote loss is undocumented.
findings.evidence: /Users/junda/robot/g1-docs/pages/09_common_istakes_and_definitions.md:67: error 'Unitree physical remote feedback data timeout'. Brief, G1 corrections: 'Keep the R3 remote bound and in a human's hand; the robot even reports an error if the remote times out'. Plan section 6: DJI Mic Mini, Lark M2, MT7612U AP; section 9: Wi-Fi fallback is 10 m Ethernet, 'the stick and button need no network'.
findings.fix: Put the AP on 5 GHz on a channel chosen from an on-site scan at setup; keep the remote within 3 m line of sight, charged, in the spotter's hand only; on Thursday test the remote with the AP, DJI, laptop and phones all radiating and log any timeout; make the wired XVF3800 (or the PTT button plus a wired handheld mic on the 10 m cable) the bench-default input if the DJI drops twice in a session, and keep the DJI for the stage.

findings.issue: The privacy card says 'no faces, no continuous recording', but the system shows a live 480x336 frame of whoever is in front on a public monitor all day, runs hand crops at 2 Hz, and stores a JPEG per memory row that will include the judge who ordered. One attendee objecting mid-demo, in a crowd that judges on privacy, is a demo-day failure.
findings.evidence: Plan section 3: brain view shows 'live 480x336 frame'; section 5: memory 'SQLite rows: t, text, vec, jpeg'; section 3 privacy card: 'no faces, no continuous recording, memory wiped at 17:00'. Brief, judging digest: winners posts praise 'privacy' and 'disciplined, non-hallucinatory design'; alternative 'Reunite' was discounted because 'a robot filming attendees all day needs sign-off'.
findings.fix: Store only the rack crop in SQLite (no JPEG of people), show the rack crop rather than the full frame on the public monitor (or blur the person region), make the card say exactly what is captured and for how long, and put a small 'camera on' sign on the table.

findings.issue: Rehearsals are realistic about noise but not about the venue, the judges or the heat. Every rehearsal is at home with crowd playback: no transport rehearsal (pack, carry, unpack, set up), no lighting variation (C920 auto white balance against a window turns the red/green/blue enum into a coin flip), a 30-minute thermal soak for a 7-hour day in a chest cavity, a 2-minute loop that assumes judges watch from 0:00 when science-fair judges arrive mid-loop (often at the staged failure at 1:15), and a 1.5 s grace window that is shorter than the confirmation line plus a human reaction.
findings.evidence: Plan section 7: Thu 'two dress rehearsals in the evening with crowd noise', Fri 'five timed stage rehearsals', Sat first contact with the venue; section 8 spike 9: '30 min under tegrastats'; section 3: '1.5 s grace window', recovery segment at 1:15 'every loop'. /Users/junda/robot/harness/LATENCY_RESULTS.md 'Known weaknesses': 'Three generated kitchens... this measures these scenes, not visual generalization'; presence gate 2/14 false positives on wide views. Brief, hackathon facts: judges 'rotate through workbenches science-fair style'.
findings.fix: Make Friday's dress rehearsal a transport rehearsal: pack the case, carry it out and back, unpack and set up against the stopwatch in a different room. Lock C920 exposure and white balance with v4l2-ctl, use saturated koozies and a matte backdrop board behind the rack, and re-score the gates on 10 frames at 09:30 on site. Run the Tuesday soak for 2 hours with temperature on the brain view and use the Damp-on-stand gaps as cool-downs. Let the presenter pick segment order per group (order and handover first; the planted failure only when a judge asks or time allows) and make the grace window 'end of confirmation speech plus 3 s' with a visible countdown, cancel on any button press with no inference.

verdict: The concept and the engineering plan are aimed correctly at this judging panel (native audio, tool calls, honest numbers, a visible recovery), so the plan can place in Track 2 if the loop runs; what would lose it is the day itself, where a free-standing 35 kg biped does handovers within arm's reach on a foam mat with an e-stop that is a fall, on one battery for a five-to-seven-hour judging window, with an untimed setup and an unrehearsed move to the stage. The single change that matters most is to run the entire bench day with the robot clipped into its protective stand, which Unitree itself recommends for demos: it turns L2+B from a fall into a hang, makes Damp between judge groups safe (the battery lever), makes the stand the dolly and the rack jig the calibration reference for the bench-to-stage move, and removes the mat. After that, order the second battery on Monday and time the setup and the move on Friday; everything else in this list is an afternoon each.
